synthesis: Recent verified developments show the major reference laboratories competing on organic volume, specialty diagnostics, workflow access and operating execution. Labcorp reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.731 billion, up 5.8%, adjusted EPS of $4.99, up 14.9%, and improved reported and adjusted operating margins of 12.1% and 15.8%, respectively. It raised enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Labcorp is also extending its consumer and specialty footprint through the 163-gene Marker hereditary-risk panel, therapy-linked oncology diagnostics and a modest local capacity expansion at its remodeled Yakima, Washington, patient service center. Quest Diagnostics continues to show stronger recent top-line momentum: second-quarter revenue rose 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue increased 10.0%, requisition volume grew 13.1% and adjusted EPS increased 19.1% to $3.12, leading to higher full-year revenue and EPS guidance. Management also disclosed the execution costs behind that growth. Revenue per requisition declined 2.8% because of mix, and Project NOVA, the Corewell Health and Fresenius Medical Care ramps, and supplemental deferred-compensation expense together reduced second-quarter margin by about 70 basis points. Quest nevertheless expects full-year margin improvement and said the Corewell relationship should contribute about $250 million of revenue with margins improving from low- to mid-single digits. Quest repurchased 522,436 shares for $100 million during the quarter and continues to expand advanced oncology access through the Flatiron Health OncoEMR integration. ARUP Laboratories remains differentiated in high-sensitivity hematopathology through its 18-marker CLARISPECT multiple-myeloma MRD spectral-flow assay, capable of detecting as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. Overall, competitive advantage is increasingly tied to combining scale and volume growth with specialized testing, embedded clinical workflows, consumer access and disciplined margin conversion.

companies.Labcorp: Labcorp is pairing improving profitability with expansion in consumer genetics, therapy-linked diagnostics and local service capacity. Second-quarter revenue rose 5.8% to $3.731 billion, adjusted EPS increased 14.9% to $4.99, reported operating margin improved to 12.1% from 11.2% and adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%. The company raised 2026 enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Marker by Labcorp adds direct consumer access to a 163-gene hereditary-risk panel covering more than 100 medically actionable conditions, supported by more than 2,200 patient service centers and genetic counseling. Labcorp also expanded its existing Yakima, Washington, footprint by adding laboratory capacity and enlarging the patient service center at 1104 W. Spruce St. The Yakima project is a local capacity move rather than a new-market entry, but it reinforces the company’s strategy of coupling national specialty capabilities with convenient specimen-collection access.
companies.Quest Diagnostics: Quest continues to combine strong organic growth with deeper integration into hospital, consumer and oncology channels. Second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue rose 10.0%, requisition volume increased 13.1% and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $3.12, prompting higher 2026 revenue and EPS guidance. The earnings call added important execution detail: revenue per requisition declined 2.8% because of mix, while Project NOVA, the Corewell and Fresenius ramps, and supplemental deferred-compensation expense together reduced second-quarter margin by about 70 basis points. Management still expects full-year margin improvement and estimates Corewell will contribute about $250 million of revenue as its margin improves from low- to mid-single digits. Quest repurchased 522,436 shares for $100 million in the quarter. Post-results analyst estimates also moved higher, but those forecasts remain external expectations. Strategically, Quest is embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR workflow and continues to broaden consumer and wellness access. A third-party FY2025 revenue classification also shows the scale of its specialty base, with gene-based and esoteric testing representing about 38% of revenue versus 54% from routine clinical testing.
companies.ARUP Laboratories: ARUP Laboratories strengthened its specialty-testing differentiation with ARUP CLARISPECT Multiple Myeloma MRD by Spectral Flow Cytometry. ARUP says it is the first large U.S. reference laboratory to offer spectral-flow technology for clinical use. The assay uses 18 markers in a single-tube design, reduces specimen-volume requirements and can detect as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. The launch gives ARUP a differentiated position in high-sensitivity multiple-myeloma MRD assessment and establishes a platform the laboratory plans to extend to additional spectral-flow MRD assays.

categories.Financials: Labcorp and Quest both raised 2026 outlooks after strong second quarters, but Quest continues to lead on recent organic and volume momentum. Labcorp revenue grew 5.8% and adjusted EPS 14.9%, while adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%. Quest revenue grew 10.2%, organic revenue 10.0%, requisition volume 13.1% and adjusted EPS 19.1%. Quest also repurchased 522,436 shares for $100 million, while its earnings call highlighted roughly 70 basis points of second-quarter margin pressure from Project NOVA, collaboration ramps and deferred-compensation expense. Labcorp’s margin expansion and Quest’s faster growth illustrate different operating strengths within the current competitive cycle.
categories.Product & Services: Labcorp’s Marker genetic-health panel brings a 163-gene, 100-plus-condition hereditary-risk offering into its direct-to-consumer OnDemand channel, while the Yakima facility expansion adds local laboratory and collection capacity. Quest is embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR workflow. ARUP launched a spectral-flow multiple-myeloma MRD assay with an 18-marker single-tube design and very high analytical sensitivity.
categories.Clinical, R&D: Recent verified activity continues to favor higher-sensitivity and therapy-relevant diagnostics. ARUP’s spectral-flow MRD assay is designed to identify very small residual multiple-myeloma populations, while Quest’s Haystack MRD workflow expansion increases community-oncology access to ctDNA-based residual-disease testing. Labcorp continues to broaden therapy-linked oncology diagnostics alongside its consumer genetics portfolio.
categories.Partnerships & M&A: Quest’s OncoEMR MPI integration with Flatiron Health and pilot with American Oncology Network illustrate a partnership model focused on embedding advanced testing directly into care delivery. Its Corewell Health relationship is expected to contribute about $250 million of revenue, with management targeting margin improvement from low- to mid-single digits as the collaboration matures. Labcorp invested $225.7 million in acquisitions during the second quarter, while its genetics expansion continues to leverage capabilities acquired from Invitae.
categories.Leadership & Organization: Quest’s recent verified organizational change remains Dominique Chokshi’s appointment as Head of Investor Relations. No newly verified leadership developments from the latest processed Labcorp or ARUP items materially changed their management structures.
